_comment: Supply-chain baseline for the OpenCode plugin roster. Every entry was measured
from the npm registry on 2026-08-20 by tools/supply-chain/audit-plugins.sh, which
compares this file against the registry on every CI run and fails on any drift.
This file is a TRIPWIRE, not a policy. It does not say these packages are safe --
it says they are the same publishers, with the same provenance posture, as when a
human last looked. A change here is not automatically an incident, but it must be
a decision: re-verify, then update this file in the same reviewed commit as the
pin bump that caused it. Never update it to silence a red build.
'maintainers' is the loudest single compromise signal in the npm ecosystem: an
account handoff has preceded most of the well-known package takeovers. It is
checked per PACKAGE (registry-wide), not per version.
'provenance' records whether the PINNED VERSION carries an SLSA provenance
attestation (dist.attestations), which ties the tarball to a CI build of the named
repository. False is not a failure -- half this roster lacks it, and a package
cannot retroactively gain provenance for a version already published. What IS a
failure is a package that HAD provenance losing it, because that means a release
stopped being built by the pipeline that built its predecessors.
Provenance proves origin, never benignity. A signed, attested tarball built by CI
from a compromised repository is still compromised.

opencode-vibeguard.note: No attestation, single maintainer, and it is the secret-redaction plugin -- so the component asked to keep credentials out of prompts is itself among the least verifiable. Pinned at 0.1.0, a pre-1.0 version untouched since. Weigh that against what it replaces, which is nothing.

@tarquinen/opencode-dcp.note: Attested. Upstream development has moved to Sleev, so treat an unfixed OpenCode-compatibility break as the trigger for an ADR on replacing it. The publishing account tarquinen previously also published @tarquinen/opencode-smart-title, removed from the roster by EOP-257, so the account now reaches one entry.

opencode-supermemory.note: Attested, and backed by a company rather than an individual. It also ships conversation content to a remote API by design, which is a data-exposure question this file does not answer.

opencode-scheduler.note: No attestation. It writes host scheduler units (launchd/systemd/Task Scheduler), so it is the plugin with the most persistent reach outside the editor process.

opencode-goal-plugin.note: No attestation, hand-published by one maintainer at six releases in ten days, and the most privileged plugin loaded: it spawns agents, writes state under .opencode/goals/ and reads whole sessions. Blueprint 12.8 names it the least-verifiable, most-privileged entry in the roster.
